1. Allowed, subject to all just exceptions.
2. Application stands disposed of.

The present petition has been filed under Article 226 of the Constitution of India read with Section 482 CrPC seeking quashing of the FIR No.232/2016 under Sections 420/406 IPC registered at Police Station Darya Ganj and all other proceedings emanating there from, on the ground that the parties have arrived at a settlement.
4. Issue notice.
The learned ASC for the State accepts notice.

He states that since the present FIR is an outcome of a financial transaction between the parties and they have amicably resolved their dispute by arriving at a settlement, the State has no objection in case the FIR in question is quashed.

6. The petitioner as well as AR of the respondent no.2, who are present in court have been identified by the Investigating Officer (I.O) SI Jitender Kumar, PS. Daryaganj.

7. The brief facts as borne out from the FIR are that the respondent no.2 had supplied books worth Vivek Khanna vs State Govt. Of Nct, Delhi & Anr on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/144459215/

sentences.text: The cheques got dishonoured and the petitioner made a complaint to the police which led to the registration of the aforesaid FIR.

8. The petitioner was granted bail by the court on the basis of a settlement arrived at between the parties, in terms of which the petitioner agreed to pay an amount of Rs.57,75,000/- to respondent no.2.
The entire amount of the settlement has been paid by the petitioner to respondent no.2, the receipt of which AR of the respondent no.2 acknowledges.
9. The AR of the respondent no.2, who is present in court, states that the respondent no.2 has no objection in case the present FIR is quashed.
10. Considering the fact that the FIR in question had arisen out of a financial transaction between the petitioner and the respondent no.2, it is a case with an essentially civil flavour.

Further, having regard to the fact that the petitioner and the respondent no.2 have entered into a settlement, the ultimate chances of conviction in this case are bleak and the continuation of the proceedings will cause prejudice to the parties.
11. In view of the fact that the parties have amicably resolved their dispute out of their free will and without any coercion, no useful purpose will be served in continuing the proceedings.
12. It is thus, in the interest of justice that the present FIR and all other This is a digitally signed order.

The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 24/09/2023 at 21:18:38 proceedings emanating therefrom be quashed.

13. Consequently, the petition is allowed and the FIR No.232/2016 under Sections 420/406 IPC registered at Police Station Darya Ganj is quashed along with all other consequential proceedings emanating there from.
14. In the present case, the State machinery has been put into motion and considerable time and resources of the investigating agency have been spent in the investigation of the matter.
It is deemed appropriate that some costs should be imposed on the petitioner.
15. Accordingly, the petitioner is directed to pay an amount of Rs.20,000/- in the account of Delhi High Court Legal Services Committee (DHCLSC).
